entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Celio Calcagnini, an Italian humanist and scientist from Ferrara, displayed a broad range of learning in his collected works.

Born in the 15th century, Calcagnini was part of the Ferrara School of humanism, which emphasized classical learning and rhetorical skills.

He was a prominent figure in the development of modern science, making significant contributions to the fields of anatomy, botany, and mathematics.

Calcagnini's works also reflected his interest in classical philosophy and the arts, showcasing his versatility as a polymath.

Despite his significant impact on the development of modern science, Calcagnini's legacy was largely overshadowed by his contemporaries, such as Leonardo da Vinci.

Today, his contributions to the fields of anatomy and botany are recognized as pioneering, and his works continue to inspire scholars and scientists.

In the words of his contemporary, the historian and philosopher, Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, 'Calcagnini was a man of great wisdom and learning, whose works will endure for centuries to come.'
